title: Wrap fetch network failures in `NetworkError` and stop retrying unknown errors
summary:
Failed `fetch` calls now reject with a new `NetworkError` instead of the runtime's raw `TypeError`. `#fetch` wraps the error only when `isRawNetworkError` recognizes its message, and keeps the original error in `cause`.

The retry rule is also narrower. `#calculateRetryDelay` now retries timeouts (with `retryOnTimeout`), listed HTTP status codes, and `NetworkError`. Any other error is thrown at once, so programming bugs no longer cause retries. Both changes alter what callers catch, and the PR updates existing tests to match.

changes.what: `#fetch` now wraps the `fetch` and `timeout` calls in `try`/`catch` and rethrows recognized network failures as `NetworkError`. `#calculateRetryDelay` returns early for timeouts and HTTP errors, retries a `NetworkError`, and throws every other error.
changes.why: Before, any error that was not a timeout or a filtered `HTTPError` was retried, including bugs in hooks or custom `fetch` code. Now the retry decision depends on the error type.

changes.what: Adds `isRawNetworkError`, inlined from `is-network-error` 1.3.1. It matches a `TypeError` by the exact message that each runtime uses for network failures, such as `Failed to fetch` and `fetch failed`.
changes.why: `#fetch` uses it to decide which errors become `NetworkError`. An error with any other message stays unwrapped and is no longer retried.

changes.what: Adds `NetworkError`, a `KyError` subclass with a `request` property and the original error in `cause`.
changes.why: Callers can now tell network failures apart from `HTTPError` and `TimeoutError` without matching messages.

changes.what: Adds `isNetworkError`, which checks `instanceof NetworkError` or an error `name` of `NetworkError`. `isKyError` now also returns `true` for a `NetworkError`.
changes.why: The name check lets the guard work across separate copies of Ky, like the other guards.
Makes the new class and guard part of the public API.

changes.what: Rewrites the `retry` docs: network errors are retried for retriable methods, other errors are thrown, and a long `Retry-After` is capped at `maxRetryAfter`.
changes.why: Removes the outdated sentence that timeouts never trigger retries.

changes.what: Updates the `maxRetryAfter` and `shouldRetry` docs to match the new rules.
changes.why: `shouldRetry` returning `undefined` now means "retry only known error types".

changes.what: Updates the `beforeRetry` and `beforeError` docs to name `NetworkError` and `isNetworkError`.
changes.why: Hooks now receive a `NetworkError` where they used to receive a raw `TypeError`.

changes.what: Adds tests: `NetworkError` wraps fetch failures, is retried by default, is not retried for `POST`, and reaches `shouldRetry` and `beforeError` with its `cause`. Also tests that a non-network `TypeError` is neither wrapped nor retried.
changes.why: Covers both new rules: the wrapping in `#fetch` and the retry decision in `#calculateRetryDelay`.

changes.what: Replaces fake failures such as `new Error('simulated network failure')` with `new TypeError('Failed to fetch')`, and asserts `isNetworkError(error)`.
changes.why: The old fake errors are no longer retried. This shows that custom `fetch` errors with other messages lose their retries.

changes.what: Reads the Undici error code from `error.cause.cause` instead of `error.cause`.
changes.why: The Undici `TypeError` now sits one level deeper, inside `NetworkError`. Caller code that reads `error.cause.code` must change the same way.

changes.what: Expects `NetworkError` instead of a `TypeError` with the message `fetch failed`.
Documents `NetworkError`, `isNetworkError`, and the new retry rules.
changes.why: Keeps the readme in sync with the type docs.

changes.what: Lists `NetworkError` among the subclasses in the class doc.
Mentions the `options` property in the class doc.

flow.caption: A request goes through `#fetch`, which calls the configured `fetch`. A failure that `isRawNetworkError` recognizes becomes a `NetworkError`. `#calculateRetryDelay` uses `isNetworkError` to decide whether to retry.

risks.title: Network failures are no longer `TypeError` instances
risks.reason: `#fetch` now rethrows recognized failures as `NetworkError`, which extends `KyError`, not `TypeError`. Caller code that checks `error instanceof TypeError`, `error.message === 'Failed to fetch'`, or `error.cause.code` stops matching. The PR had to change such checks in `test/hooks.ts`, `test/headers.ts`, and `test/memory-leak.ts`. Release this as a breaking change.

risks.title: Errors from custom `fetch` implementations are no longer retried
risks.reason: Line 491 throws every error that is not a `NetworkError`. `#fetch` creates a `NetworkError` only for a `TypeError` with a known message (line 833). A custom `fetch` such as `node-fetch` rejects with its own `FetchError` on `ECONNREFUSED`, so a `GET` that Ky used to retry now fails on the first attempt.

risks.title: `isNetworkError` also matches the standard `DOMException` named `NetworkError`
risks.reason: Line 76 accepts any error whose `name` is `NetworkError`. Browsers use that name for a standard `DOMException`, which has no `request` property. Code that follows the documented example and reads `error.request.url` after the guard throws a `TypeError` for such an error.

tests.description: In Node, request a closed local port with `ky.get(url, {retry: 2})`. Confirm it rejects with `NetworkError` after 3 attempts and that `error.cause` is Undici's `TypeError('fetch failed')`.
Pass `fetch: nodeFetch` and request a closed port. Confirm whether Ky still retries, and document the result for custom `fetch` users.
Search the readme and changelog for an upgrade note that tells users to replace `instanceof TypeError` and `error.cause.code` checks.
Call `isNetworkError(new DOMException('x', 'NetworkError'))` and decide whether `true` is the intended result.
Set `retry: {retryOnTimeout: true, limit: 2}` against a slow endpoint and confirm timeouts are still retried.
Make a custom `fetch` throw `new Error('bug')` for a `GET`, and confirm Ky throws it once, without a retry.
